title: Free fermionic black holes as polarised mirrors
summary: Understanding the speed with which various classes of quantum systems can scramble information is a key goal of quantum information theory, with relevance to both fundamental physics and the study of the efficiency of quantum algorithms. Famously, such understanding enabled Hayden and Preskill to show that, under the assumption that black hole dynamics may be modelled by a Haar-random unitary, old black holes act as ''mirrors'', reflecting infalling quantum information back out again effectively instantaneously. In this work, we investigate which aspects of this mirror behaviour survive…
